How to stick to a routine
when motivation is gone
Make it so small you can't fail. Two push-ups, one page, five minutes. On bad days, the tiny version keeps the habit alive until motivation comes back.
Attach it to something you already do. After coffee, read. After brushing your teeth, stretch. Habits stick better when they ride on old ones.
Never miss twice. Missing one day is human. Missing two days starts a new habit of quitting. Get back on track the very next day, even with the tiny version.
Prepare the night before. Gym bag by the door, book on the pillow, running shoes out. Removing friction makes starting almost automatic, even on lazy days.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A small, enjoyable habit teaches your brain that routines can feel good.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A small, enjoyable habit teaches your brain routines can feel good.

slides.texte_overlay: Track it where you can see it. A calendar on the wall, crosses for every day done. Not wanting to break the chain is a surprisingly strong force.
Focus on identity, not results. Not "I want to run a marathon" but "I'm a runner." When it's who you are, showing up feels natural and easy.
